sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: 11.1 L30 directly states tendons connect muscles to bones. The qualifier «обычно» matches the general anatomical role rather than claiming every tendon attachment without exception. Muscle/skin is a real facial-muscle relationship at L47, not the usual tendon definition; bone/bone and bone/cartilage are articulating-structure relationships at9.1 L30/L34/L35, not the tendon muscle/bone pair. Exactly one usual attachment answer among four parallel anatomical pairs. Key1 is evidenced by the primary claim, not the frozen index.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: 11.1 L30 explicitly says tendons are strong bands of dense regular connective tissue and transmit contraction-generated skeletal-muscle tension to the skeleton. L33 and L62 explain bone motion by these attachments. Both sentences accurately teach tissue, force transfer and movement; directly naming tendons explains the key through the muscle-to-bone pathway instead of a generic label. Two sentences below70 words; no blanket claim that all muscles move bone (L47/48 exceptions).

defects.kind: Russian anatomical term/scope in two distractor notes
defects.finding: The source describes fibrous and cartilaginous joints in the broad English sense of articulation (9.1 L34–38). CURRENT translates these as «в некоторых суставах» and «в хрящевом суставе». In Russian anatomical usage сустав denotes the movable/discontinuous articulation; the cited English category explicitly includes immobile skull sutures atL40 and immobile/slightly mobile cartilage articulations atL38. These notes therefore carry the same unqualified scope transfer independently visible in their own literal text. The limited «в некоторых» in note2 does not establish a new source claim about fibrous tissue within a narrower synovial joint.
